name: Racing Green
lede: Racing green is a very dark green tied in popular memory to British racing cars.

sections.title: A car color
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines racing green as the dark green of the British racing car of the 1920s [1]. St Clair gives a similar gloss, a dark evergreen associated with early British car racing [2]. Paterson also files it in its list of greens [1].

That is about all the books say, and it is enough to place the name: it is a twentieth-century, motor-sport name rather than a pigment or dye name [1][2]. Neither book explains why green became the national racing color, so this page does not either [1][2]. Like many names in this dictionary, it records a use more than a recipe, so it has no single pigment behind it [1]. What the books agree on is the era and the country, the 1920s and Britain [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #014600 is almost a pure, very dark green with little else in it [3]. It sits close to [[dark-green]], [[hunter-green]] and [[forest-green]] [3]. Screen colors are approximate, and real car paint varied with the maker and the year [3].

notes.cite: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "racing green", pp. 330, 499
St Clair, The Secret Lives of Colour, "Racing green"

questions.q: What is racing green associated with?

openers: Racing green is the dark green of 1920s British racing cars.
